# What If America Almost Had Universal Healthcare?

The United States stands as a global anomaly—the only developed nation without a government-mandated form of comprehensive health coverage.

While peer nations established universal systems to protect citizens from medical bankruptcy, the U.S. remains tethered to a fragmented private system defined by high administrative costs and crippling medical debt. 

# So why? How did America become the exception?

The usual answers are comforting, familiar, and mostly wrong.

We’re told it’s because Americans value “freedom.”\
Or because our system is too complex.\
Or because universal healthcare is politically impossible here.

But those explanations assume something that isn’t true:

> That the system we have is the result of a natural, democratic choice.

It isn’t.
